channel.title: The Imaginative Conservative - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Imaginative Conservative (theimaginativeconservative.org)

item.title: When Mother Teresa Came to Washington
item.description: As I looked around that room in Washington, filled with so many powerful people, I realized that one day in Mother Teresa’s life brought more good to the face of the earth than all our efforts combined for a lifetime. (essay by Barbara J. Elliott)

item.title: Optimizing Human Fulfillment
item.description: A well-ordered society requires the presence of three essential relationships: man's connection to the world, to one another, and to God. (essay by Regis Martin)

item.title: Waiting for Odysseus: The Tale of Argos
item.description: As enticing as Odysseus’ adventures are, questions remain: what of Penelope, Telemachus, Laertes, and indeed Ithaca left behind? What about their twenty years without a King, a father, a husband, and a son? Odysseus’ brief encounter with his faithful dog Argos demonstrates the price paid by those left behind. (essay by Winston Elliott)

item.title: The Domestic Monastery: The Rule of Saint Benedict
item.description: Whatever a person’s place in life, Saint Benedict offers a “little Rule for beginners.” The principles of the spiritual life which he sets down put us down firmly in life right where we are. By paralleling family and monastery, today’s reader can glean simple yet practical wisdom for, as well as extraordinary insight into, the essence of everyday Christian living. (essay by Dwight Longenecker)

item.title: Robert Fagles: A New Voyage With Odysseus
item.description: From the Greek dramatists to Joyce and Kazantzakis, the character of Odysseus has continued to fascinate. Robert Fagles has done such a superb job in his translation of "The Odyssey" that perhaps not since Homer has this epic hero seemed both so grand and so human. (essay by John Rees Moore)

item.title: Roman Concord: St. Clement of Rome’s Famous Letter
item.description: The Letter of Clement provides our first glimpse of the Gospel fused with 'Romanitas'—a vision of Rome not so much as a symbol of strength and power as of unity and peace. Whereas the old 'Pax Romana' was achieved through conquest and force, the new order would be built on the love of Jesus. (essay by Michael De Sapio)

item.title: "Adelaide"
item.description: Beethoven wrote "Adelaide," a song for solo voice and piano, when he was in his mid-twenties. The theme of the poem that provides the text for the song—the yearning for an unattainable woman—would indeed become the animating theme of Beethoven's love life. (song by Ludwig van Beethoven)

item.title: Paul Kingsnorth's "Against the Machine"
item.description: Paul Kingsnorth believes that the Machine Age has replaced the four P's of traditional culture (the past, the people, place, and prayer) with four S's: science, self, sex, and the screen. (essay by Chuck Chalberg)

item.title: Four Hours of Fury: The Story of World War II's Operation Varsity
item.description: The Rhine River was the line of no return—once the paratroopers of the 17th Airborne crossed it, they’d be over enemy territory. Some pretended to sleep while others smoked or just stared into space. No one spoke. The roar of the engines and the rattling of the airframe made conversation impossible, which was just fine. Most were dwelling on their own thoughts anyway. (book excerpt by James M. Fenelon)

item.title: How to Pray in Mystical Contemplation
item.description: The offering of ourselves that we make is a “true” and therefore acceptable offering when it is made with a “pure and humble heart”. When we learn to thank, praise, adore and glorify him for who he is and for what his love has done for us, then we are learning the meaning of true selfless loving. (essay by David Torkington)
